subject: health
unitTitle: Media, Technology, and Digital Influence on Health
title: Explicit model: influencer marketing, sponsorship disclosure, and undisclosed advertising
focus: influencer marketing, sponsorship disclosure, and undisclosed advertising
essentialQuestion: Who profits when I believe a health claim, and how do I check before I share it?
keyPoints: Influencer marketing may use sponsorships, affiliate links, gifts, or personal brands; disclosure shows an incentive but does not by itself prove or disprove the claim.
Check authorship, expertise, evidence, currency, uncertainty, and incentive before using a health message; confidence, popularity, and testimonials are not substitutes for support.

For influencer marketing, sponsorship disclosure, and undisclosed advertising, a strong response distinguishes fact from assumption, uses a fictional or public case, and includes a safe next step or appropriate source of support.
privacySafeScenario: Take apart three fictional but realistic health posts: identify the claim, the incentive, the evidence actually offered, and what a reliable source says instead. Write the correction you would actually post.
studentTask: Compare two supplied fictional messages about influencer marketing, sponsorship disclosure, and undisclosed advertising. Build a four-row check for source or author, evidence, date or context, and incentive; then choose the stronger message, cite two details, and state what remains uncertain.
knowledgeCheck: In two or three sentences, explain the most important distinction in influencer marketing, sponsorship disclosure, and undisclosed advertising; use one lesson fact and name the evidence, safety check, or support route that makes the explanation dependable.
completionCriteria: The response completes every named part of the influencer marketing, sponsorship disclosure, and undisclosed advertising task using the supplied fictional or public case.
The response uses at least two accurate details from the lesson instruction and distinguishes evidence from assumption.
The response gives a safe, feasible next step or support route and does not depend on private disclosure, body comparison, or recorded media proof.
adaptationChoices: Teardowns may be written, spoken, annotated on printouts, or completed on a supplied four-column template. No account creation, login, or live platform use is required.
extensionChallenge: Apply influencer marketing, sponsorship disclosure, and undisclosed advertising under a new constraint, compare two approaches, or explain the idea to someone else with an original fictional example, without completing another learner's graded work.
